verdict.rationale: Foreloop's docs say that nothing runs until a person approves a contract, which is described as the only gate before an agent changes the repository. An agent proposes the tasks, the intention carries editable deliverables, and agents only claim approved tasks, so a human reviews and approves before any code changes. Missing for 10: detail on what an approved contract contains as an implementation plan (steps or files touched; the docs note you need not know which files change), and independent or hands-on corroboration of the approval gate.

support.subject: As a developer, I can review and approve an agent's implementation plan before any code changes are made

citations.quote: Nothing runs until a person approves a contract. Approval is the only gate, and the gate is deliberate: an agent is about to change your repository.
That agent asks Foreloop for approved tasks in that repository, claims one, does the work, and opens a pull request from your GitHub account.
its agent reads the submission, fills in the intention, and proposes the tasks
An intention adds an agreed purpose and editable deliverables when you need more clarity.
